definitions.explanation: An unfavorable fortune or outcome. Most commonly encountered on omikuji fortune slips, where it indicates bad luck. Also used more broadly to mean something ominous or inauspicious.

examples.japanese: おみくじ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{凶|きょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}た→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: I got bad luck on my omikuji.
I drew bad luck, so I tied it to a tree.

examples.japanese: {凶|きょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}て→出る：00513_deru⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{気|き}にしない→気にする：03026_kinisuru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦いれば→いる：00495_iru⟧、⟦もう{一度|いちど}→もう一度：02976_mouichido⟧{引|ひ}き{直|なお}す⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Some people don't worry about drawing bad luck, while others draw again.

notes:
Bad fortune or ill omen, most commonly seen on omikuji fortune slips at shrines and temples. The opposite of ⟦{吉|きち}→吉：19344_kichi⟧.

OMIKUJI CONTEXT:
When someone draws {凶|きょう}, the custom is to tie the paper slip to a designated tree or rack at the shrine, symbolically leaving the bad luck behind. Some shrines have eliminated {凶|きょう} from their omikuji to keep visitors happy.

COMPOUNDS:
- ⟦{大凶|だいきょう}→大凶：25063_daikyou⟧ — terrible luck (worst possible result)
- ⟦{凶悪|きょうあく}→凶悪：28175_kyouaku⟧ — atrocious, heinous
- ⟦{凶器|きょうき}→凶器：16384_kyouki⟧ — weapon (used in a crime)
- ⟦{凶作|きょうさく}→凶作：16485_kyousaku⟧ — crop failure, bad harvest
- {凶事|きょうじ} — misfortune, calamity

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{不吉|ふきつ}→不吉：16952_fukitsu⟧ — ominous, unlucky (adjective-like usage, broader range)
- ⟦{災難|さいなん}→災難：04161_sainan⟧ — disaster, misfortune (an actual event, not a prediction)
